subject.title: [Bug]: xAI/Grok "could not decrypt encrypted_content" 400 trips the per-model circuit breaker (no auto-recovery)

question: Should maintainers accept pre-fix production logs plus source-level positive/negative coverage as sufficient proof for the linked xAI/Grok retry fix, given the provider-side rotation cannot be induced on demand?
rationale: The remaining blocker is proof acceptance for a real but non-client-inducible provider error shape; code inspection shows the bug and the linked fix path, but automation cannot create the xAI rotation event.

options.title: Accept source-level proof for this case
options.body: Review the linked PR on code, tests, and redacted pre-fix logs, with after-fix organic logs added later if xAI rotates again.

options.title: Wait for organic after-fix proof
options.body: Keep the linked PR blocked until a future xAI rotation produces redacted after-fix gateway evidence.

options.title: Require a broader breaker design
options.body: Defer the narrow fix and open a separate provider-error classification design before changing this recovery path.

recommendation.title: Accept source-level proof for this case
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR on code, tests, and redacted pre-fix logs, with after-fix organic logs added later if xAI rotates again.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owned the adjacent encrypted-reasoning retry fix in the same transport predicate and is the strongest history-backed proof-sufficiency routing candidate.
